environment.instrument_bias_source: workstream B/GB, 13 House-G-US corpus cycles with results attached

governor.no_control_stake: 36 governorships confer no collective majority, so there is no control probability to report -- only how many are won.

prior_asserted.why: the House prior sigma times a ratio of 1.75 that has never been measured. Every other sigma in this model is fitted. No source publishes statewide governor returns in the shape the fit needs: MEDSL's tidy 1976-2024 series is President, Senate and House only.

bound.range_source: the per-cycle spread of the Senate ratio measured in engine/backtest/senate_prior.py — 2.2763 / 0.8891 / 1.1998
bound.verdict: the whole plausible range moves the median by nothing and the expected count by 0.05 governorships

prior.source: engine/backtest/fit_prior_sigma.py — prior-only residuals pooled over 2018, 2020, 2022 at every horizon
prior.chamber_ratios_note: house 1.0 by construction. SENATE IS ASSERTED AND NOW TESTED (engine/backtest/senate_prior.py): measured at 1.465 on 97 Senate races against 1202 House districts over 2018, 2020, 2022, clustered se 0.420. The asserted value is kept because the measurement does not disagree with it — three cycles of Senate maps cannot separate the two — not because it was never checked. Re-run the module when a fourth cycle exists. GOVERNOR IS STILL ASSERTED AND UNTESTED: MEDSL's governor file is behind a Dataverse guestbook, and governors are cut from the model.

senate_ratio_fit.sigma_house_note: the DENOMINATOR of the ratio, measured under a realised environment; not PRIOR_SIGMA and not a substitute for it

votehub_races.used_for: every candidate-level poll in the model

electindex_gb.used_for: the national environment, and so the prior for 465 unpolled races

movement.note: Each cause is an exact re-run, not a linearisation. The range is the two orderings: these effects are not additive, and where the range is wide the causes cannot be separated.
